content.failureBehavior: Block release when authored content, links, policy assertions, or focused application behavior fail.

graph.failureBehavior: Block release when scene, markdown, graph, search, or textbook routing manifests are stale or invalid.

size.failureBehavior: Block release when the exact load-time resource closure changes without review or exceeds its declared uncompressed source ceiling.

visual.method: Inspect current desktop and phone-width browser captures at the exact declared viewports.
visual.failureBehavior: Block release for overlap, clipping, illegible hierarchy, unusable wrapping, hidden required actions, or unexplained horizontal overflow.

browser.method: Exercise declared interactions on a loopback preview and record console output and required runtime state.
browser.failureBehavior: Block release for a console error, missing public dependency, failed required interaction, unsafe navigation, or wrong runtime schema.

accessibility.method: Check accessible names, unique identifiers, landmarks, heading structure, keyboard-focusable controls, focus visibility, and declared control-size floors.
accessibility.failureBehavior: Block release when any required control is unnamed, duplicated, unreachable, visually unfocusable, or smaller than the profile floor.

preview.method: Build the candidate from an isolated clean checkout plus the scoped candidate files, verify inclusion in the static payload, and exercise the route over loopback HTTP.
preview.failureBehavior: Block release when the isolated build, route, required public dependencies, or source-bound browser evidence does not pass.

rollback.method: Bind the candidate to the incident runbook and one accepted last-known-good site identity whose same-environment reconstruction is repeatable.
rollback.failureBehavior: Block release when no explicit last-known-good identity or tested reconstruction exists. A live production rollback remains a separately authorized mutation.

size.scope: entrypoint plus recursively discovered load-time CSS and JavaScript only
size.exclusions: User-selected GitHub issue navigation and the three shared public JSON manifests are recorded as interactions or public data dependencies, not code in this source-byte envelope.

requiredInteractions: load all three same-origin public manifests
strip query and fragment from the supplied public route
expose the public issue link without submitting it

rollback.firstReleaseBoundary: The last-known-good site predates feedback.html, so a rollback deliberately removes the new route while restoring the prior accepted site.
